findings.resolution: Startup pg_catalog options precede SQL; initial identity uses qualified built-in catalogs only; canonical catalog comparison precedes supported schema-version read on new/reused/readiness paths. Actual TLS tests prove marker executability, zero native marker execution on refusal, and restoration.

review_notes: R3 requires origin at identity/baseline and refuses non-origin before DISCARD ALL; no application replication-mode repair or parameter grant.
R4 startup path and built-in qualification prevent metadata or shadow catalog use before canonical comparison; post-catalog version check also runs for ordinary recycle and readiness.
The metadata-view and shadow-pg_roles regressions have positive execution controls and test new and reused sessions for every fixed role, zero marker writes, and operator-restored readiness.
The version1 regression confirms the structural v2 catalog is unchanged and accepted before native schema-version refusal, then verifies recovery.
Independently executed 18 library tests, one compile-fail public-construction doctest and 35 real local PostgreSQL16.13/TLS checks with unchanged author-pinned inputs plus ADR004.
Author Rust1.85 floor, strict clippy and production-library receipts inspected but not independently repeated in this supplement.

Catalog normalization/schema Python correctness remains independently owned by schema review. Root retains final binary HTTP/image/CI and managed RDS checks. No hosted identity, application write, tenant admission or ticket completion claimed.
